title.narrative: South Sudan Provision of Essential Health Services Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to increase access to an essential package of health services and respond to health emergencies in the Republic of South Sudan, with a particular focus on the former states of Upper Nile and Jonglei

The development objective of the Provision of Essential Health Services Project is to increase access to an essential package of health services in the Republic of South Sudan, with a particular focus on the former states of Upper Nile and Jonglei. The project has three components. First component, Delivery of Essential Health Services will support the provision of a defined package of essential health services, targeting the populations of the former states of Upper Nile and Jonglei, and other vulnerable communities affected by conflict and violence; Second component, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning will finance costs related to a national unified monitoring approach (co-financed with DFID and HPF3), as well as specific monitoring of project activities in areas accessible for independent monitoring; Third component, Emergency Preparedness and Response will support the national EVD Preparedness and Response Plan. UNICEF is currently providing surge technical support that participate in the multi-sectoral National and State Task Forces (in high risk areas) as well as technical working groups; and Fourth component, Repayment of Project Preparation Advances will also support the repayment of Project Preparation Advances from other projects that were disbursed but for which the projects were never delivered due to the country context following the July 2016 crisis.

comment.narrative:

By 30-June-2021, ten state-level Rapid Response Teams trained on investigation of alerts and immediate outbreak response. This represents a 200% achievement of the revised 5 end target value.???????</p>

title.narrative: Number of health facilities providing at least 75 percent of the essential package of health services

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Target not achieved</strong>. During the AF, the end target date was revised from 31-Jan-2021 (original) to 31-Dec-2021 to align with the project's closing date. By 30-June-2021, a total of 128 health facilities was providing at least 75 percent of the essential package of health services (<em><strong>ICRC:</strong> 19/20; <strong>UNICEF:</strong> ?109/191</em>). This represents a 64% achievement of the 200 end target value.???????</p>
<p>Achievements in this indicator was hindered by the introduction of MoH standardized incentives for health workers in May 2019, resulting in large-scale strikes; seasonal flooding that limits beneficiary accessibility to health facilities; challenges recruiting and retaining qualified health staff willing to work in remote locations; major rehabilitation restrictions, resulting in the inability to address infrastructure gaps; weak IP capacity; and limitations in PEHSP’s financial envelop with some health services reliant on other stakeholders for delivery (e.g. PMTCT, HIV/ AIDS, family planning). </p>

title.narrative: Number of health facilities with essential medicines available

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Target partially achieved</strong>. During the AF, the end target date was revised from 31-Jan-2021 (original) to 31-Dec-2021 to align with the project's closing date. By 30-June-2021, a total of 147 health facilities had essential medicines available (<em><strong>ICRC:</strong> 20/20; <strong>UNICEF:</strong> ?147/191</em>). This represents a 74% achievement of the 200 end target value. </p>
<p>Achievement of this indicator was hindered by delays in pharmaceutical distribution due to heavy seasonal flooding, critical lack of warehouse space that limits the amount of supplies that can be prepositioned in the field (impacting rainy season preparedness), lack of temperature control in health facilities (affecting pharmaceutical efficacy due to poor storage conditions), lack of space to accommodate essential drugs and medicine equipment (resulting in increased risk of theft andlooting); inadequate stock management by IPs at health facility level, and long lead times for procurement due to COVID-19. </p>

title.narrative: People who have received essential health, nutrition, and population (HNP) services

comment.narrative:
<p>As this PDO indicator is a HNP CRI, the CRI is a composite indicator calculated by the summation of three sub-indicators  (“<em>Number of children immunized</em>”; “<em>Number of women and children who have received basic nutrition services</em>”; “<em>Number of deliveries attended by skilled health personnel</em>”). Since PEHSP’s projectpreparation, that task team has treated the CRI indicator as five separate indicators, instead of one composite indicator. For the purposes of the ICR, the ICR will evaluate the CRI PDO indicator according to the CRI definition as no alternative definition has been provided in the PAD, and has hence revised the original end target and results to align with the CRI definition.</p>

<p><strong>Target surpassed</strong>. During the AF, the end target date was revised from 31-Jan-2021 (original) to 31-Dec-2021 to align with the project's closing date. By 30-June-2021*, a total of 958,873 people (<em><strong>ICRC:</strong> 503,053; <strong>UNICEF:</strong> ?455,820</em>) had received essential health, nutrition, and population (HNP) services as defined by the HNP corporate indicator (CRI) definition. This represents a 320% achievement of the 300,000 end target value. The number of females who have receivedHNP services as defined by the CRI definition is 592,871 (61.8%). All other CRI sub-indicators have exceeded their original end targets.</p>

<p>The ICR author would also like to acknowledge the cumulative number of people who have received HNP servicesby 30-June-2021 and not limited by the CRI definition is 3,458,275 (<em><strong>ICRC:</strong> 937,815; <strong>UNICEF:</strong> ?2,520,460</em>). This would have represent a 247% achievement of the original 1,400,000 end target value. The number of females that have received HNP services and not limited by the CRI definition is 1,564,107 and would have represented a 196% achievement of the original 800,000 end target value.</p>

<p><em>*As part of the project design, planned activities had an implementation period of approximately 2 years </em><em>(from March 11, 2019 to June 30, 2021), with the closing date designated to December 31, 2021 to allow six months for financial closure by ICRC and UNICEF</em></p>
